stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Bulldozer action planned on Asad's home in Ghaziabad; Rahul slams government over CBSE re-evaluation process more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. Rahul Gandhi slams govt over CBSE re-evaluation costs says, 'Beware of pickpockets' Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday questioned the Centre and the CBSE over the answer sheet verification and re-evaluation process. In a post on X, he wrote, “Students are being forced to pay extra money just to ensure that their own answer sheets are evaluated correctly. If marks are wrongly awarded due to a CBSE error, why should students and their families bear the burden?” 2. Bulldozer action proposed against murder accused's house; notice served in Ghaziabad Five days after Class 11 student Surya Chauhan’s murder in Ghaziabad’s Khoda area, authorities served a notice on the house of main accused Asad’s father, alleging illegal occupation of government land. Officials warned of demolition action if the encroachment is not removed within 15 days, while police continue searching for the absconding accused. 3. Yogi's remark on merit list sparks attention; 223 UP toppers honoured Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath honoured 223 Class 10 and 12 state board toppers in Lucknow, joking that girls dominate merit lists because boys are busy with household chores. He also urged students to avoid excessive smartphone use and focus on learning and discipline. 4. Commercial LPG cylinders costlier by up to ₹53.50 Commercial LPG cylinder prices have been increased by up to ₹53.50 from June 1, adding to operating costs for restaurants, hotels and catering businesses across the country. The price revision comes as part of a series of changes taking effect at the start of the month. 5. UP plans 6 nuclear power plants to meet rising electricity demand Uttar Pradesh plans to set up six nuclear power plants with a combined capacity of 8,400 MW to meet growing electricity demand. Most projects are proposed in Purvanchal, with NTPC, IOC and the Adani Group showing interest. The state is also preparing its first nuclear power policy. 6. Mayawati launches BSP comeback drive, reaches out to former leaders BSP chief Mayawati has begun efforts to bring back former party leaders and strengthen the organisation ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The move aims to rebuild the party’s Dalit, Muslim and Brahmin support base, with several former MPs and MLAs reportedly in touch with the BSP. 7. Iran says US clearly not complying with ceasefire Iran’s Parliament Speaker and lead negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has accused the US of breaching its ceasefire agreement with Iran, including by continuing its blockade of Iranian ports and failing to restrain its ally Israel from escalating attacks in Lebanon. 8. Devkinandan Thakur says Hindu lives have become ‘cheaper than petrol’ Religious preacher Devkinandan Thakur sparked controversy during a discourse in Gujarat, claiming that the lives of Hindus and cow slaughter have become “cheaper than petrol and diesel”. Referring to the Ghaziabad murder case, he called for greater Hindu unity and also welcomed Muslim groups reportedly supporting the demand to declare the cow as ‘Rashtra Mata’. 9. Thunderstorm, rain alert in 63 UP districts; winds may reach 70 kmph The weather department has issued a yellow alert for thunderstorms and rain across 63 districts of Uttar Pradesh, with wind speeds expected to reach 40–70 kmph. Recent storms claimed two lives in Lucknow and Lakhimpur Kheri, while hailstorms and heavy rainfall brought relief from heat in several districts. 10. South actress makes allegations against Tamil Nadu CM says, 'He was responsible for my miscarriage' South actress and former Bigg Boss South contestant Julie has leveled several serious allegations against actor and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Thalapathy Vijay. She has held Vijay and his party, TMK is responsible for her miscarriage.

stories.title: AAP MP Sanjay Singh clashes with officials in Prayagraj:Asks, 'Is discussing paper leaks a crime?'; two student leaders detained
stories.summary: In Prayagraj on Monday, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh had a heated confrontation with ADM City Satyam Mishra and DCP Manish Kumar Shandilya. Singh was interacting with students at the Circuit House on alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations when the two officials arrived with police personnel and sought to halt the programme. ADM City Satyam Mishra asked Singh to step aside for a discussion, prompting a sharp response from the AAP leader. Criticising the officials, Singh said: “Am I disrupting law and order that you have come here to stop me? Is discussing paper leaks a crime? You have no authority to enter the Circuit House. Had I been holding a programme on a public road or at a public venue, you could have intervened. You are attempting to undermine the rights and privileges of a Member of Parliament. I will raise this matter before the Privileges Committee.” Singh remained seated and refused to leave the venue. The officials eventually moved to another room in the Circuit House, while he continued his interaction with students on examination-related issues. However, moments later, as Singh stepped outside to address the media, the power supply to the hall was reportedly switched off. Power supply cut during media interaction After the meeting ended, Sanjay Singh stepped outside to speak to the media. According to him, the electricity supply in the hall was cut off at that time. He expressed displeasure over the administration's actions and said such discussions could not be stopped. Two student leaders detained Police detained student leaders Pankaj Pandey and Ashutosh Pandey, coordinators of the United Competitive Students Hunkar Manch. Ashutosh was present at the Circuit House during the event, while Pankaj was detained near Jahaj Chauraha in the Karnalganj area. Both had participated in a student protest held on May 29. Students angry over recruitment exam irregularities Students in Prayagraj have been protesting against alleged irregularities in the UP Daroga and Lekhpal recruitment examinations. On May 29, more than 2,000 competitive exam aspirants staged a demonstration, alleging paper leaks and demanding greater transparency in recruitment exams. The students demanded the release of the UP Daroga recruitment scorecard, cancellation of the Lekhpal examination, transparent recruitment processes, and strict action against those involved in paper leak cases. They have also announced a "Chalo Lucknow" march on June 12. Three coaching institutes sealed after protest Following the May 29 demonstration, authorities sealed three coaching institutes—Exampur Wala Coaching, Super Climax Coaching, and Target On Coaching—alleging involvement of their teachers and students in the protest. Commenting on the action, Sanjay Singh accused the government of trying to divert attention from examination-related failures. He said the focus should be on ensuring fair and transparent examinations rather than taking action against coaching institutes.

stories.title: Rape survivor climbs tower with 3-year-old tied to her back:Alleges police inaction despite FIR; descends after 6 hours on DM's assurance
stories.summary: A rape survivor climbed an 80-foot-high mobile tower in Uttar Pradesh's Gonda district on Monday with her three-year-old son tied to her back, alleging that police had failed to arrest the accused despite an FIR being registered. The incident triggered panic in the area and drew a large crowd. Senior officials, including the ADM and ASP, reached the spot and spent nearly six hours persuading the woman to come down. She finally descended after District Magistrate Priyanka Niranjan assured her that action would be taken. Climbed tower with son tied using saree According to locals, the woman, a resident of a village under Tarabganj police station limits, entered the premises of Raghukul Vidyapeeth School around 9 am. She tied her son to her waist with a saree and climbed the mobile tower installed on the campus. She sat at a height of about 50 feet and refused to come down despite repeated appeals from police and administrative officials. Woman alleges accused still at large During the rescue operation, the woman spoke to CO City Anand Rai over the phone from the tower. She alleged that a man from her village had raped her and that although an FIR had been filed, the accused had not been arrested. She further claimed that the accused continued to harass her and that she had repeatedly approached police and senior officials seeking action. Police send water and biscuits for child Concerned for the safety of the child, police personnel climbed partway up the tower and provided water and biscuits. Fire brigade and police officials remained engaged in talks with the woman for several hours. The woman told officials that she had made multiple visits to Gonda and Lucknow regarding her complaint and had submitted several applications to the authorities. Descends after DM's intervention Police also arranged a video call between the woman and the accused's mother, who urged her to come down and assured support. However, the woman remained adamant. The standoff ended only after District Magistrate Priyanka Niranjan personally spoke to her and assured her that appropriate action would be taken. Following the assurance, the woman safely climbed down from the tower along with her son.

stories.title: Wife gets life term for acid attack on husband:Sambhal court also imposes ₹1.75 lakh fine; victim lost eyesight in both eyes
stories.summary: A court in Sambhal on Monday sentenced a woman to life imprisonment for throwing acid on her husband's face and eyes, leaving him permanently blind. The court also imposed a fine of ₹1.75 lakh on the convict. Additional District Judge Gopal delivered the verdict after holding Kahkashan guilty in the case. The judgment came after more than a year of court proceedings and 10 hearings. According to the prosecution, the incident took place on March 7, 2025, in the Sadar Kotwali area. Muzaffar Ali had allegedly caught his wife, Kahkashan, with her lover at their home earlier that day. Following an argument, Muzaffar went to sleep at night. The prosecution said Kahkashan later threw acid on his face and eyes while he was asleep. The attack severely burnt his face and parts of his shoulder and stomach. He also lost vision in both eyes. Photos after the incident… Victim treated for six months in Delhi Muzaffar Ali was admitted to Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi, where he underwent treatment for nearly six months. Despite prolonged treatment, doctors were unable to restore his eyesight. Special Public Prosecutor Narendra Kumar Yadav told the court that a day before the acid attack, Kahkashan had allegedly mixed poison in her husband's food in an attempt to kill him. He claimed some relatives had also supported her in that act, though no FIR was lodged in that matter. Convict breaks down after sentence After the court pronounced the sentence, Kahkashan broke down in tears. Police later took her into custody and sent her to jail. During the proceedings, she kept her face covered with a dupatta. Muzaffar Ali also attended the hearing along with his mother. Due to injuries from the acid attack, he kept his face covered with a towel. Love marriage in 2019; couple has two children Kahkashan, 30, a resident of Bijnor district, had married Muzaffar Ali, 35, in a love marriage in 2019. The couple has two children, a five-year-old daughter and a two-and-a-half-year-old son. According to the prosecution, Muzaffar had objected several times to his wife's alleged relationship with another man living near their home. Defence to challenge verdict in higher court Kahkashan's lawyer, Pinky Sharma, said the defence was not satisfied with the judgment and would challenge it in a higher court. She questioned the delay in registration of the case and alleged that Kahkashan had been targeted because of her love marriage. The defence also claimed it was not given adequate opportunity to present its arguments before the court. Bail cancelled after conviction During the trial, Kahkashan's bail plea was rejected by the sessions court in June 2025. She later secured bail from the Allahabad High Court. However, after convicting her on May 27, the court cancelled her bail and ordered that she be sent to jail.

stories.title: 'Boys are busy with household chores, girls dominate merit lists':Yogi felicitates UP board toppers in Lucknow; 223 students from 75 districts awarded
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath honoured students who secured top positions in Classes 10 and 12 during a state-level merit ceremony at Lok Bhawan in Lucknow on Monday. During his address, Yogi made a light-hearted remark, saying that girls are appearing more frequently in merit lists because boys seem to be occupied with household chores such as sweeping, mopping and buying vegetables. A total of 223 students from 75 districts who secured places in the top 10 of the state merit list were awarded medals and certificates. Among them were 85 boys and 138 girls. Similar felicitation programmes were also organised across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh, where 1,459 meritorious students were honoured. Parents and school principals of the toppers were also felicitated. Along with UP Board students, toppers from CBSE, ICSE and the Sanskrit Education Board were included in the programme. 6 Important Points from Yogi's Speech 1. Exams should build confidence, not fear Yogi said examinations should be designed to boost students’ confidence rather than create fear. He said question papers should not be so difficult that students become nervous. He added that a good teacher is not one who troubles students with unnecessarily difficult questions. According to him, some teachers who set such questions often struggle to answer them themselves. He said the situation in the education system was quite different nine years ago. 2. Avoid giving smartphones to young children The Chief Minister said parents are a child’s first teachers. He expressed concern over the growing habit of handing smartphones to children as young as two or three years old whenever they cry. He advised parents to engage children in activities that encourage creativity instead. Yogi said education is much broader than literacy and that India has a rich tradition of knowledge and learning. 3. Followers do not matter in interviews Yogi urged students not to pressure their parents into buying smartphones. He said the government has already provided tablets to students and encouraged them to use these devices for learning. He advised students to read newspapers and watch news programmes but avoid spending excessive time on social media. According to him, 10 to 15 minutes, or at most half an hour, is sufficient. He said social media often distracts people and offers limited useful content. “No interviewer will ask how many followers you have,” he told students. 4. Students once came from Punjab to cheat in exams Recalling the past, Yogi said cheating was widespread in examinations nine years ago and merit had little value. He claimed that students from Punjab used to travel to eastern Uttar Pradesh to take advantage of the situation. He said there were instances where one person appeared in an examination on behalf of another. He also noted that teacher recruitment was inadequate and school conditions were poor. According to him, the situation has improved significantly. Today, examinations for around 56 lakh students are completed within 14 to 15 days, results are declared within a similar period and marksheets are distributed on time. Earlier, the process used to take three to four months. 5. Do not assume you know everything The Chief Minister said confidence is important, but students should never believe they know everything. He warned that overconfidence often leads people to ignore small but important details, which can eventually result in failure. Yogi encouraged students to work with honesty and clear intentions. He stressed the importance of practical knowledge and understanding India’s traditions. He said there is no shortcut to success and that hard work never goes to waste. 6. Give importance to physical health Yogi said it is not necessary for everyone to become a doctor, engineer or civil servant. Students can also contribute to society as social workers and in many other professions. He encouraged students to gain knowledge about their chosen fields and continue learning throughout their lives. Referring to the ongoing summer vacation, he advised them to use the break productively. The Chief Minister also stressed the importance of maintaining physical health through proper sleep, balanced meals and a disciplined routine. He urged students to develop a sense of responsibility towards society and the nation.

Officers arrested two suspects at the scene; a third is being traced. They claim officers coerced the girl into making a video statement against her mother, before pushing them away from the post. Police later conducted a medical examination but, the family says, sought to pre-shape the narrative. stories.title: IPL final betting racket busted in Varanasi, 11 held:Police uncover ₹25 crore operation linked to Mumbai bookies
stories.summary: A seemingly ordinary flat in Varanasi turned out to be the nerve centre of a high-value IPL betting operation, with police claiming that wagers worth around ₹25 crore were placed on the IPL final alone. Acting on specific intelligence, the Special Operations Group (SOG) and Cantt Police raided a flat in Taktakpur late on Sunday night, breaking open the door before arresting 11 people, including nine alleged bookies from Mumbai. Tracking suspicious activity According to the SOG, intelligence inputs about large-scale betting during the IPL had been under investigation for several days. During surveillance, officials received information about suspicious activity inside a flat located in a residential colony in Taktakpur. Investigators also found that several outsiders were staying at the premises despite having no apparent connection with Varanasi. After verifying the information and finding the circumstances suspicious, a joint police team conducted a late-night raid on May 31. Network spread across states Police said all 11 arrested individuals were linked to a betting network. Of those detained, two are residents of Varanasi while nine are from Mumbai. Preliminary findings suggest the group was operating betting activities linked to the IPL final between Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Gujarat Titans. Investigators believe the operation catered to bettors across multiple states. Key findings so far: • Betting worth nearly ₹25 crore was allegedly handled during the IPL final. • Eleven suspects were arrested from the flat. • Nine of those detained are residents of Mumbai. • The network reportedly had links in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Delhi. Secret digital operation uncovered The investigation revealed that the accused avoided conventional phone calls and instead relied heavily on encrypted and digital communication channels. Police said several secret and VIP groups had been created on Telegram and WhatsApp. Through these groups, the suspects allegedly coordinated betting activity and remained in touch with clients across the country. Why Varanasi became the base According to the SOG, the syndicate deliberately chose Varanasi instead of major metropolitan cities such as Delhi, Mumbai or Chennai. Investigators believe the city was used as a safe house because the operators considered the risk of detection to be lower. Police suspect betting worth several crores was conducted throughout the IPL season, with the Taktakpur flat functioning as a command centre for bookies operating nationwide. Accounts under scrutiny Officials are now questioning all the accused and examining their financial records. A formal case is being registered and the arrested individuals are expected to be sent to jail. Investigators are scrutinising bank accounts to trace the movement of funds and identify beneficiaries. Police sources indicate that the probe could potentially reveal links to influential individuals. Items recovered during the raid include: • Sophisticated laptops and tablets • Android and keypad mobile phones • Voice recorders and internet routers • Digital betting registers • Cash, passbooks and ATM cards • Accounts allegedly opened using fake identities Police believe transactions worth crores were routed through these accounts and say the investigation remains ongoing.

stories.title: Bulldozer action proposed against murder accused Asad’s house:Notice served by authorities; Asad buried hours after encounter
stories.summary: Five days after the murder of 17-year-old student Surya Chauhan in Khoda, Ghaziabad, a heavy police presence remains in the area to maintain law and order. On Sunday, Surya’s family immersed his ashes in the Ganges at Haridwar. Family members, relatives, and workers from several Hindu organisations accompanied the family during the ritual. Members of these organisations have continued to visit Surya’s home and extend their support to the bereaved family. Meanwhile, the main accused in the case, Asad, was killed in a police encounter. His body was buried late on Saturday night. Citing security concerns, police did not reveal the exact location or timing of the burial. Three accused, including Asad’s father, Nawab, have been sent to jail, while the fifth accused remains absconding. Police teams are conducting searches to trace and arrest him. Preparations to run bulldozer on Asad's father's house In the Navneet Vihar area of Khoda, the administration took action on Monday and pasted a notice on the house of the accused Asad's father, Nawab. The administration team reached the spot, and a notice issued by the SDM was put up on the main gate of the house. To inform people, the administration had drums beaten, and announcements were also made through loudspeakers. The administration stated that the land on which the house is built has been illegally occupied. The notice states that Asad's father must submit his response to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) office within 15 days. He has also been asked to remove the illegal occupation himself. The administration has warned that if the encroachment is not removed within the stipulated time, the administration will take action itself and demolish the house. The entire cost incurred in the action will also be recovered from the concerned person. The Tehsildar remained present at the spot during the action. A heavy police force was also deployed to deal with any situation. A large number of local people also gathered at the spot to witness this action by the administration. Stabbed repeatedly with knife on Eid day Surya Chauhan was a class 11 student. He was associated with the Hindu Raksha Dal. On May 28, on Bakrid, Asad reached the street with his companions. He called and said he would show the sacrifice of a goat. Surya said what do I have to do with it. To which Asad said he would show how a goat is halal slaughtered. In lane number-2, Navneet Vihar, Asad, along with his father and three others, surrounded Surya and stabbed him repeatedly. CCTV footage of this also came to light. As soon as the family got information and reached the spot, they immediately took Surya to the hospital. Then, on May 29, Friday, Surya died in a Noida hospital. More than 500 people created a ruckus for 10 hours After Surya's death, on May 30, Saturday, at 8 am itself, more than 500 people took to the streets. They raised slogans against the murderer. Demanding an encounter, they said that just as our Surya has gone, the murderer should be killed in an encounter. In front of Surya's mother, the neighborhood women had said that we don't want food. We want death for death. The family members had refused to perform the last rites, demanding an encounter with the accused. The commotion continued for about 10 hours, and people calmed down after police officers persuaded and assured them. The last rites of the body were performed at Delhi's Ghazipur cremation ghat around 6 pm in the presence of police. Asad was killed in encounter The main accused in Surya's murder, Asad, who had a reward of ₹50k on him, was killed by police in an encounter on the morning of May 31. While Asad's father, Nawab, and Asad's friends Farhan and Aatif were sent to jail. A panel of 3 doctors conducted the post-mortem of Asad's body on Sunday. After which, only his uncle came to collect the body. Asad's family members are absconding, and the house is locked. ACP Abhishek Srivastava informed that Surya's body was buried in Ghaziabad at night. Former MLA from Meerut will arrive today BJP leader Sangeet Som, former MLA from Sardhana in Meerut, will reach Surya's house in Khoda today. He has given a sharp reaction regarding the Surya murder case that occurred in Ghaziabad. Posting on social media, he said, "Those who are taught in their upbringing that Laden and Baghdadi are servants of Allah, they will never talk about humanity". Sangeet Som further said that those who are 20% today make sacrifices; if they become 40%, they will commit massacres. It may be noted that today at 12 o'clock, Sangeet Som will go to Surya's house in Ghaziabad.

stories.title: Lok Adalats cannot grant divorce decrees:Allahabad HC says, 'Interference in family court's jurisdiction not lawful'
stories.summary: The Lucknow Bench of the High Court has clarified in a significant decision that the Lok Adalat or the District Legal Services Authority has no authority to grant a divorce decree. The court stated that the jurisdiction to grant a divorce decree lies only with the Family Court, and Lok Adalats are limited to facilitating settlements; they cannot deliver judicial decisions. This decision was given by the Division Bench of Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice AK Chaudhary on a petition in which a woman challenged an order passed by the Unnao District Legal Services Authority in 2018. The husband had considered the said settlement as a divorce and made it the basis for remarriage. Freedom to remarry legally unacceptable The court stated that, according to the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, and the National Legal Services Authority (Lok Adalat) Regulations, 2009, divorce-related matters cannot be referred to Lok Adalat for adjudication. The function of Lok Adalat is only to attempt settlement between the parties, not to judicially resolve disputes. The court expressed serious displeasure at the action of the Legal Services Authority, Unnao, stating that when the law itself prohibits Lok Adalats from granting divorce, passing such orders amounts to exceeding jurisdiction. The court also said that mentioning in the settlement that both parties are free to remarry is legally unacceptable and illegal. Adalats should not enter the domain of regular courts The court clarified that till date, no decree of divorce has been duly passed by a competent court between the parties; the husband's claim that the said settlement is grounds for divorce cannot be considered legally valid. The court said that Lok Adalats are an important medium for a speedy and accessible justice system, but they must function within the limits of their jurisdiction. They should not enter areas reserved for regular courts. While disposing of the case, the High Court granted the petitioner woman the freedom to take appropriate action as per law and directed that a copy of the order be sent to all Lok Adalats and District Legal Services Authorities of the state for future compliance and guidance.

stories.title: Expansion of IT City in Lucknow:LDA to include excluded lands in the scheme; 2 lakh families to get houses
stories.summary: The scope of the proposed IT City project in Lucknow will now expand further. This ambitious project, being developed over approximately 3,490 acres, will now also include those lands that were previously left out of the acquisition process. For this, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has started the process of preparing a separate land acquisition proposal. Lands adjacent to the project area and previously left out for various reasons are being identified. These include some land reserved for Ansal API's Sushant Golf City project. LDA believes that to prevent any kind of obstruction in future development works, no plot adjacent to the project boundary will be left out. Land adjacent to these villages will also be included Under the project expansion, preparations are underway to include land adjacent to the boundaries of several villages, including Sonai Kanjehara, Pahadnagar Tikariya, Parehta, and Sikandarpur Amoliya. After obtaining plot-wise records and maps of the concerned villages, the acquisition proposal will be sent to the government. The LDA's acquisition department has asked the Chief Town Planner and related officials to provide gate-wise DPR and land details. After receiving the documents, a separate proposal for the acquisition of the remaining lands will be sent to the government. Officials say that to develop the IT City in an integrated manner, it is necessary to include the entire perimeter in the plan.

stories.title: CM Yogi Adityanath to visit Gorakhpur tomorrow:2-day visit planned; development projects worth over ₹300 cr to be unveiled
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will arrive in Gorakhpur on Tuesday afternoon. He is coming on a two-day tour. In two days, he will give gifts of development projects worth more than ₹300 crores. This includes projects related to tourism development, industry and housing. The Chief Minister will reach Gorakhpur on Tuesday afternoon after attending a program organised in Kushinagar district. He will reach Chiluatal at 4 pm in the evening. The work of tourism development and beautification of Chiluatal Ghat has been completed there. According to Deputy Director of Tourism Department Rajendra Prasad Yadav, a project worth ₹20 crore 39 lakh has been given concrete shape to develop Chiluatal as a tourist destination. The works carried out by UP Projects Corporation Limited as the implementing agency include construction of a 570-meter pathway, construction of ghat steps, railing along the lake shore, solar lights, interlocking, CC road, benches, 400 meters approach road, 500 meters side wall and drain construction, gate superstructure work, crate boulder and stone pitching, shop, toilet block construction, etc. With the development of Ramgarh Tal's boating facilities, the beauty of Chilua Tal is emerging prominently. People have started coming for morning and evening walks. After this, the CM will go to Gorakhnath Temple. There, he will hold a meeting with officials and review the progress of development works ongoing in the district. Presentations on future plans will also be made before the CM. On Wednesday morning, the CM will listen to the problems of complainants who come to the public darshan organised at Gorakhnath Temple. After that, at 11 AM, they will reach Gorakhpur Industrial Development Authority (GIDA). There, they will inaugurate this factory built at a cost of ₹42 crore 50 lakh. It will provide readymade garment facilities on a plug-and-play basis. Approximately 80 entrepreneurs will be allotted space here. On this occasion, CM Yogi will also inaugurate the LIG-EWS residential complex in the GIDA industrial area and present development works worth approximately ₹208 crore as a gift.

stories.title: UP Metro to implement 'One Nation, One Card':One card for all metro networks; available at any station nationwide
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation (UPMRC) is going to launch the National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) service from June 15. After its implementation, passengers will not need to keep separate cards for metros in different cities. A single card can be used for metros and other public transport services in many cities across the country. The NCMC card will now replace UPMRC's existing smart card. Old cardholders can also exchange their cards for a new card. Through this card, passengers will be able to travel not only on Lucknow, Kanpur, and Agra Metro but also on all metro networks where the NCMC facility is available, including Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Bengaluru. This will eliminate the need to buy a new ticket or card while traveling in other cities. According to Metro officials, NCMC will not be limited to metro travel only. It can also be used for bus travel, parking fees, toll tax payment, and retail shopping. This card can also function as a prepaid, debit, or credit card, which will depend on the issuing bank. The card has been given NFC-based contactless technology, through which passengers will be able to make payments just by tapping. It will also have an offline transit wallet facility, due to which the fare will be automatically deducted at the metro station entry and exit gates even without internet. This will speed up passenger movement and reduce crowds at stations. NCMC cards will be made available to passengers before June 15 through designated counters and partner banks.

stories.title: AI Cameras to be installed at 'Blind Spots' of Kashi:Security Committee made recommendation, SDM says, 'Devotees from 137 Countries arrived within a year'
stories.summary: Preparations have begun to further tighten the security arrangements of Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple and its grand corridor. In addition to the AI-based cameras and security equipment already present in the premises, new and state-of-the-art cameras will now be installed at some identified 'blind spots'. However, the security committee has only recommended this so far. But this matter is already pending with the government. Currently, 325 CCTV cameras are installed in the temple, all of which are operational. Blind spots have been identified in the temple SDM Shambhu Sharan stated that the temple administration is extremely serious about security. He said that CCTV and AI-based cameras are already installed throughout the entire perimeter of the temple. However, our permanent security committee has proposed installing some more cameras at certain blind spots and in view of the increasing number of devotees. In consideration of that proposal, the temple trust is contemplating taking action so that more cameras can be installed from a security perspective and according to better technology. Flood of faith pouring in even in scorching heat ADM Shambhu Sharan stated that the record-breaking heat in North India is not affecting the enthusiasm of Baba's devotees at all. Currently, one and a half to two lakh pilgrims are bowing their heads daily at Baba Vishwanath's court. Meanwhile, on weekends (Saturday and Sunday), this figure increases to around 2 to 2 and a half lakh, which is a big record in itself. 30 crore devotees visited in 4 years, people arrived from 137 countries SDM said that since the inauguration of Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in December 2021, a new chapter of tourism and faith has begun in Kashi. Sharing the statistics, the ADM informed that in the last four years, approximately 30 crore devotees have received the blessings of Mahadev at Kashi Vishwanath. The growing global acceptance of Kashi can be gauged from the fact that in just the last year, citizens from 137 countries have paid their respects at Baba's court. stories.title: Devkinandan says 'Hindu lives cheaper than petrol':Claims Muslims are now protesting for cows, calls it 'Kalyug'
stories.summary: 'In the country, there are two things cheaper than even 1 liter of petrol-diesel: First, cow slaughter, and Second, the lives of Hindus. Just now in Ghaziabad, a 15-year-old child was stabbed. Anyone comes kills Hindus and leaves. Hindus themselves are responsible for this.' These words were spoken by storyteller Devkinandan Thakur on Sunday. These days, his religious discourse is ongoing in Gujarat. Speaking during the event, he said that people often remain preoccupied with concerns about their own future, while the Hindu community is gradually diminishing. He stressed the need for greater unity and awareness within society. Referring to the political slogan "Batoge Toh Katoge" (If divided, you will be weakened), he said such concerns are usually raised during election periods. He added that governments should enact laws after elections to prevent divisions in society and ensure that the Hindu community remains secure and united. ‘Now Muslims also demand that cow be declared ’Rashtra Mata' Devkinandan Thakur's Katha, which started on May 29 in the Somnath Temple premises, will continue till June 4. On Sunday, Devkinandan said that, currently, some surprising events are being witnessed. Until now, Hindus have been used to saying that the cow should be declared ‘Rashtra Mata’. Now, Muslim brothers are also saying from mosques that the cow should be declared the ‘Rashtra Mata’. They are also agitating for this. They are making announcements everywhere. The question is, who is stopping this from happening now? We feel that perhaps this is the Kaliyuga. Thanked Muslim community from the Vyasa Peeth Devkinandan Thakur thanked Muslims. He said that for the first time from our pulpit, gratitude is being expressed to those Muslim brothers who have openly demanded that ‘Gaumata’ (Cow) be declared 'Rashtra Mata'. He described this initiative as a positive step towards Hindu sentiments. He said that such thoughts should be respected. Such thinking should be encouraged in society, which will strengthen unity and harmony. Everyone should move forward together in the direction of declaring the cow as 'Rashtra Mata'. Raised demand for Sanatan Board earlier, too During the Mahakumbh, storyteller Devkinandan Thakur had come into the limelight by raising his voice for a Sanatan Board in the country. By talking about Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi and organizing a Dharm Sansad, he had garnered support from saints. He had said that, not to grab land like the Waqf Board, we want a Sanatan Board to save temples. We cannot even save our own temples. Is this the rule of the Mughals in the country? Now, know who Devkinandan Thakur is? Devkinandan Thakur was born on September 12, 1978, in Ohawa village of Mathura in a Brahmin family. His father's name is Rajveer Sharma, and his mother's name is Ansuiya Devi. Devkinandan Thakur's mother had deep faith in the Srimad Bhagavad Gita. He also has 4 brothers and 2 sisters. His original name was Devki Prasad Sharma. Devkinandan's childhood was spent in quite ordinary circumstances. Facilities like Tempo did not reach his village. Due to this, to catch the bus, he had to walk about 6 kilometers with his family. At just 6 years of age, he left home and reached Vrindavan. There, he got the opportunity to join Braj's Raslila institution. In Raslila, he played the roles of Lord Shrikrishna and Lord Ram. After playing the role of Shrikrishna, he came into considerable discussion. This is considered the beginning of his spiritual life.

stories.title: 'Muslims defamed by Surya's killing on Bakrid':Family seeks strict action; police hunt absconding suspect
stories.summary: “The Bakrid-day murder sent a message across the country that a Muslim youth had lured a Hindu teenager to his home and killed him. The action taken by the police and the government was justified, and we are satisfied with it.” This is what Mohammad Imran, a resident of Khoda in Ghaziabad, says. On May 28, on the day of Bakrid, Asad (20), along with his friends, stabbed and murdered Surya Pratap Singh 'Surya' (17), a class 11 student. On Sunday, the police killed Asad in an encounter. When the 'Dainik Bhaskar' team reached the spot, they found that there was only a 300-meter distance between Surya's and the main accused Asad's homes. While there was mourning at Surya's house, Asad's house was found locked. Police from 8 stations are deployed within a one-kilometer radius. RRF personnel are patrolling the area. Asad's father, Nawab, along with 3 accused, has been arrested and sent to jail. One accused is still absconding. Surya's mother said that the fate that befell Asad should also befall all the accused. Local people fear that the police might kill the other accused in an encounter. Therefore, they are avoiding speaking openly. They were not even ready to point out the houses of the accused. In Khoda, with a population of about 15 lakh, there is peace for now, but the tension has not completely ended. People's eyes are now fixed on the police's next action. Read the ground report... First, know the profile of all the accused... Lock hanging on Asad's house, uncle took the body Asad's flat in Lokpriya Vihar in Khoda is on the first floor of a 4-storey building that has a lock hanging on it. There is a mosque nearby. Barriers have been placed at intervals to prevent crowds from reaching Asad's house. Police personnel are alert here. On Sunday, after the post-mortem, uncle Abid received the body. He said, Asad, had made a mistake, for which he has been punished. His company was also not right. He used to work at a cloth shop. We are residents of Bulandshahr. We will perform the last rites in the village. Know what the neighbors said... 'As Asad did, so happened to him too' Mohammad Imran lives in the neighborhood of the accused Asad. He says that the murder of Surya happened near our house. Asad's house is in the adjacent lane. Asad's encounter was right. We have been demanding since the first day that the boy who committed such a heinous crime should meet the same fate. It was Bakrid, a festival day. Asad has defamed the Muslim community. Ikramuddin said - What Asad did, the same happened to him We met Ikramuddin nearby. He said, we were busy at our home on Bakrid that day. Curtains were put up outside the house. That's why I couldn't see the murder happening. On the question of Asad's encounter, Ikramuddin said, Surya's mother's demand was that there should be an encounter. She had said that blood should be avenged with blood. That's why Asad's encounter happened. What happened, happened for the good. Just as Asad had done wrong, the same happened to him. Here, an attempt was made to spoil the atmosphere in the wrong way. 'Everyone equally guilty in Surya's murder' Former BJP Municipal Vice President Chaman Singh Chauhan said that I know Surya's family. This family is also our neighbor in the Etah district. The Yogi model has been seen here. Asad had committed a heinous crime here. There was an altercation between Surya and Asad 8 months ago. Surya was a Hindu boy. The police encounter was justified. If you watch the video footage, others are equally guilty in it. The one who gave the knife should also be encountered. Ankit Tyagi said- Surya was very good Ankit Tyagi's house is in front of Surya's house. Ankit said that Surya's father died about 18 months ago. Surya's elder brother, Yash Chauhan, remains mentally ill. All the responsibility of the house was on Surya. Never heard of Surya having any dispute with anyone. Surya's family's financial condition is very weak. The house rent is ₹6k. There is no earning member in the house. The second son remains ill. The atmosphere here is not right; whoever is involved in this murder of Surya, the police should take strict action against all of them. Surya's mother said - All murderers should be encountered After the murder of Surya Chauhan, his mother Saroj is in a terrible state from crying. There was a crowd at their house. People from Hindu organizations were present. Women from the neighborhood were seen consoling Saroj. We spoke to Surya's mother. She said that after my son's death, even the tears have dried up from my eyes. Elder son Yash himself remains ill. Younger Surya was killed. In this incident, the police killed Asad. Three have been caught. One is still absconding. The police should encounter all the murderers. On, UP government's help, Saroj said that yes, the government has provided financial assistance and assured employment. Just as I have become homeless, he should also become homeless. Today, I don't have a roof over my head; my only prayer to Yogiji is that those who murdered Surya should also not have a roof over their heads. Bulldozers should run over their houses. Markets remained closed for 2nd consecutive day on Sunday On Sunday, RRF and the police force remained deployed at the main gate in Khoda. Considering the tense atmosphere, barriers were put up, and vehicular movement was completely restricted. Police force kept conducting flag marches all around. Markets in Khoda remained closed for the second consecutive day as well. ACP Indirapuram Abhishek Srivastava and ACP Sahibabad Amit Saxena remained present with the force. There was only crowding in the lane where Surya Chauhan's rented house is located. Apart from this, silence prevailed in all other lanes. Khoda has a 75 percent Hindu population, while 25 percent are Muslims. Accused Farhan told policemen - I had given the knife to kill Surya The arrested accused Farhan told police during interrogation that I was friends with Atiq, Sarik, Asad, and Surya. On May 28, around 3 pm in the afternoon, Asad had a fight with Surya over riding a bike. Asad had told this to his father, Nawab, and me. Then we made a plan to teach Surya a lesson, and half an hour later, at 3:30 pm, we cornered Surya in Navneet Vihar lane number 4. I gave the knife to Asad, and Asad's father said finish his story today. Then Asad stabbed Surya in the stomach. When Surya fell down covered in blood, we all thought he was dead and left from there. SP spokesperson said- Surya had a relationship with Asad's sister

stories.title: 6 new nuclear plants to maintain electricity shortage in UP:Most plants planned for Purvanchal; State currently has only 1 nuclear power plant
stories.summary: UP has the highest electricity demand in the country. To meet this, the government is going to set up 6 nuclear power plants. Of these, National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) may build 3, Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) 2, and Adani Group 1 power plants. These will be plants with a total capacity of 8,400 megawatts. Currently, UP does not have any policy for nuclear power plants. The government is also going to bring a new policy for setting up new power plants. A draft is being prepared for this. It will soon be brought to the cabinet for approval. Of the new plants that are going to be built in UP, 3 have been allocated to Purvanchal. Western UP and Bundelkhand have received 1 each. The site for 1 other plant is yet to be decided. Currently, UP has only one nuclear power plant at Narora in Bulandshahr. NTPC has submitted proposals for 3 plants An official from the Energy Department says that NTPC has shown interest in setting up plants in Prayagraj, Lalitpur, and Sonbhadra. The company has submitted detailed proposals for this. All projects propose two reactors of 700-700 megawatts each, with a total capacity of 1,400 megawatts. Additionally, the initial feasibility assessment of NTPC's proposed sites has been completed. Meanwhile, survey and evaluation work is ongoing at IOC's sites. Both NTPC and IOC will work on a Joint Venture (JV) model with government companies that are experts in the nuclear energy sector. However, which districts Adani Group wants to build plants in has not been made public by the company. Project may take 9 years to complete Sources associated with this project say that this project is currently in its initial phase. It is difficult to specify any fixed timeline right now. For a nuclear power plant, approvals need to be obtained at multiple levels. After receiving all necessary clearances, it typically takes 7 to 9 years to build the plant. These sites for the plant have been selected keeping in mind water, land, and better grid connectivity. In the feasibility study, local impact, seismic zones, and environmental balance are also being given full attention. Demand for 32 thousand megawatts of electricity in UP Another official from the Energy Department says that the demand for electricity in UP has reached around 32 thousand megawatts. In the coming years, this could reach 40 to 45 thousand megawatts. For this, a supply of clean baseload power is necessary apart from coal-based plants, solar, and hydro power. Nuclear energy can be the best option. Nuclear plants generate electricity 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Their carbon emissions are negligible. Distribution of electricity will be according to need What will be the share of the center and state in the 6 nuclear power plants to be built in UP? This has not been decided yet. The distribution of electricity will be decided according to need and demand. However, the state in which the power plant is installed usually gets more electricity compared to other states. It is the responsibility of the state government to provide land and water for the nuclear plant. While technology, environment, and nuclear safety-related approvals will be under the central government and the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board. Narora Nuclear Plant is producing 440 MW of electricity The Narora Atomic Power Plant, located on the banks of the Ganga River in Bulandshahr, has a capacity of 440 MW. Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has been operating it since 1991. This plant has generated 3,000 to 3,500 million units of electricity in recent years. This is 85% of the plant's total capacity. Narora Power Plant is UP's first nuclear power center, which was built using Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) technology. The electricity generated here is supplied to Delhi, Haryana, and the Northern Regional Grid in addition to UP. However, the estimated cost of all six projects, required land, timeline for commencement of construction, and potential date of power generation have not been made public yet.

stories.title: Yellow alert for thunderstorms and rain in UP's 63 districts:Winds will blow at speed of 40-70 km/h, hail fell in Amroha; Basti remains warmest city
stories.summary: There is an alert for storms and rain in 63 districts on Monday in UP. Winds will blow at speeds of 40 to 70 kilometers per hour. Meanwhile, in the past 24 hours, there has been rain with strong winds in districts adjacent to NCR. Hailstones fell along with rain in Amroha. Heavy rain with strong winds occurred in Lucknow, Sambhal, Moradabad, Hathras, Gonda, and Balrampur. Meanwhile, light to moderate rain occurred in Shahjahanpur, Firozabad, Farrukhabad, Aligarh, and Bulandshahr. On Sunday, 34.4 mm of rain was recorded in Ballia, 21.8 mm in Moradabad, 19.4 mm in Hardoi, 3 mm in Hamirpur, 2.4 mm in Agra, 2.4 mm in Lucknow, and 2 mm in Lakhimpur Kheri. In Lucknow, a 10-year-old child who was bathing outside the house during the rain died when a wall collapsed. In Lakhimpur Kheri, a 7-year-old child lost his life when a mud wall collapsed during a heavy storm and rain. Meanwhile, in Rampur on Saturday evening, during the storm, an iron tin shed of a hotel broke loose and fell on a youth riding a bike, leaving him seriously injured. There was a decline in maximum temperatures across all districts, including Bundelkhand. The Basti region remained the hottest, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 40°C. In Orai (Jalaun), 39.8°C, in Banda, 39.2°C, in Varanasi, 39°C, in Prayagraj, 38.6°C, and in Jhansi, 38.3°C, temperatures were recorded. From June 2, the weather will change again. Heat will show its intensity. The mercury will rise by 4°C to 5°C. However, there are no signs of heat waves. See 2 pictures from Sunday

stories.title: Mayawati plans ‘Ghar Vapsi’ of former BSP Leaders:BJP, SP leaders reconnect with BSP; will it reshape opposition politics?
stories.summary: Mayawati has begun efforts to bring back former BSP leaders, issuing two key directives in recent meetings. First, party coordinators have been asked to reach out to influential regional leaders and bring them into the BSP fold. Second, the party is focusing on reconnecting with veteran leaders to help retain its shrinking vote base. Amid speculation of a possible BSP-Congress alliance, sources say several former MPs and MLAs from Western UP, Awadh, and Purvanchal are in touch with the BSP. Many of them are reportedly concerned about losing election tickets or being denied candidacies by their current parties. Most are former legislators, and sources indicate that some could join the BSP within the next two to three months. BSP's alliance will be with Congress or smaller parties On May 20, two senior Dalit leaders of Congress reached Mayawati's house in Lucknow. They were Barabanki MP Tanuj Punia and Rajendra Pal Gautam, National President of Congress's Scheduled Caste Department. However, Mayawati did not meet these leaders. Actually, neither BSP nor Congress has made any formal announcement regarding the alliance yet. It is being speculated that even if there is no alliance with Congress before the elections, Mayawati may still enter the electoral field by forming an alliance with smaller parties. BJP benefits from BSP's strengthening, SP faces loss Both SP and BJP have become alert due to the activism of BSP. Akhilesh Yadav is working on the PDA (Backward, Dalit, Minority) formula. However, BSP's comeback may lead to division in Dalit and Muslim votes. BJP is relying on its OBC and Hindutva politics. However, if Mayawati's Brahmin outreach increases, it may have an impact on some seats. At the same time, the strengthening of BSP may pose the biggest threat to SP. Because BSP's effort will also be to draw the Muslim vote bank towards itself. In the last two elections, the 2022 Assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha, a large portion of the Muslim vote bank has remained with SP. In such a situation, if there is a division of Muslim votes, SP will suffer direct losses. BJP could benefit the most from the division of votes. Will Mayawati try the 2007 formula again? In 2007, BSP formed a government with an absolute majority through the social equation (social engineering) of Brahmin-Dalit-Muslim and backward classes. Mayawati is now trying to repeat the same formula in 2027. In recent meetings, she has assigned responsibilities to her trusted leaders- Apart from these, all coordinators have been asked to form Muslim Brotherhood committees within 3 months. Mayawati believes that the neglected sections under the BJP and SP governments are now turning towards the BSP. Expert says- Old leaders know the party's weaknesses Senior journalist Syed Qasim says- 'Jatav face Jai Prakash Singh, who was expelled 7 years ago for comments against Rahul Gandhi and the Prime Minister, has been taken back into the party. This step by Mayawati is being seen as part of a strategy to strengthen the Dalit vote bank and include experienced leadership in the party. Meanwhile, former MLA Wahab Chaudhary was expelled from BSP in March 2026 on charges of anti-party activities. However, in May itself, his expulsion was revoked, and he was brought back into the party. Wahab Chaudhary has a good influence in the Muradnagar area of Western UP. Syed Qasim says that Mayawati is giving priority to leaders who played a key role in the 2007 victory. Old leaders know the party's weaknesses very well. Their return will not only strengthen the organization, but will also bring new enthusiasm among workers. Leaders who left BSP before the 2024 elections In 2019, BSP had 10 Lok Sabha MPs. Most of these leaders had switched sides before the 2024 elections. Leaders who left BSP during and after the 2022 Assembly elections Lalji Verma and Ram Achal Rajbhar, these two leaders were once considered the strongest pillars of BSP and Mayawati's very close strategists. They were expelled from the party just before the 2022 UP Assembly elections. After that, both joined the Samajwadi Party. Then they became MLAs on SP tickets. Azamgarh's prominent leader Guddu Jamali also left BSP and joined SP. He was later sent to the Legislative Council (MLC) by SP. Imran Masood has changed several parties, but came to the BSP for some time. Then, after expulsion, he joined Congress. Leaders cited these reasons for leaving BSP- Lack of communication with leadership- Several MPs (like Ritesh Pandey) said that for a long time, there had been no direct meeting or conversation with the party high command (Mayawati). Ticket denial or reshuffling- Due to BSP's strategy of denying tickets to old MPs and giving opportunities to new faces, many grassroots leaders also switched sides.

stories.title: 27,000 names deleted from Panchayat election list:3rd phase verification completed, final list to be published on 10th
stories.summary: In the three-tier panchayat elections, around 27,000 names are being deleted from the voter list after the completion of the third phase of verification of suspected duplicate voters. Month-long verification drive completed During nearly a month-long verification exercise, officials found around 27,000 individuals whose names appeared not only in their respective gram panchayats but also in two or more other gram panchayats within the district. A consolidated list has been prepared, and these names are now being removed. The final voter list will be published on 10 June. Special revision and voter count changes Along with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the voter list for panchayat elections was also revised. The draft list published earlier had a total of 29.88 lakh voters, while after SIR the number rose to around 31 lakh. This led to a situation where the number of voters in gram panchayats and the overall district (including urban local bodies) appeared nearly equal, raising administrative concerns. Large-scale duplication checks conducted Since SIR data could not be questioned, the panchayat voter list was re-examined. Initially, BLO-level scrutiny identified around 30,000 duplicate entries. The State Election Commission then sent a list of 5.16 lakh suspected duplicate voters, prepared at block level. BLOs were instructed to enter the last four digits of Aadhaar numbers for verification. After this process, 1.51 lakh voters were found to be duplicate, bringing the total identified duplicates in the first round to about 1.81 lakh. However, due to the addition of nearly 2 lakh new voters, the final list remained largely unaffected. Second large list sent for verification Later, the State Election Commission sent another list containing 12.37 lakh suspected duplicate voters, this time prepared at district level. After Aadhaar-based verification through BLOs, 1.27 lakh duplicate voters were identified and removed from the list. Third list still under verification When officials believed the process was complete, another list surfaced containing 11.33 lakh suspected duplicate entries, also prepared at district level. So far, 62% of this verification has been completed, and around 14,000 duplicate voters have been identified in this phase.

stories.summary: The administration in Varanasi has completed preparations for the three-day UP Police recruitment examination scheduled from 8 to 10 June. A total of 1.32 lakh candidates will appear in the exam, which will be conducted at 50 schools designated as examination centres. Exam to be held in six shifts The examination will be conducted in two shifts per day, making it a total of six shifts across three days. The first shift will be held from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon, while the second shift will take place from 3:00 pm to 5:00 pm. At each of the 50 centres, 22,032 candidates will appear in every shift. A large number of security personnel will be deployed at the examination centres. Police, STF, LIU, intelligence units, and several other agencies will also monitor the examination process. High-level coordination meeting held A joint coordination meeting was held at the Police Lines auditorium to ensure a smooth and transparent conduct of the examination. Officials discussed preparations in line with government directives.The District Magistrate informed that all arrangements have been completed for the exam scheduled from 8 to 10 June. He also stressed the need for inter-departmental coordination given the large scale and sensitivity of the examination. Focus on law, order and logistics Discussions were held on maintaining law and order and smooth traffic management during the examination days. Key areas reviewed included security arrangements, smooth entry and exit of candidates, crowd management around centres, traffic and parking arrangements, public facilities, electricity and water supply, sanitation, and emergency services. Arrangements were also discussed for railway stations, bus stands, major intersections, and areas surrounding examination centres. Officials present in meeting The meeting was attended by Additional CP Shivhari Meena, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar, SP (EOW) Pradeep Kumar, Additional Commissioner Alok Kumar Verma, ADCP Namrata Srivastava, ADM Rajesh Kumar and Govind Singh, DIOS Bholendra Pratap Singh, along with other departmental officials, zonal and sector magistrates, police officers, and examination centre in-charges.

stories.title: Dimple Yadav bows before Shankaracharya, seeks apology:Says SP chief stands with him; nature will avenge the insult
stories.summary: Badri Nath Jyotish Peeth Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand reached Mainpuri on Friday with his “cow protection yatra”. Here, Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav met him. She bowed before him, sought his blessings, and also presented him a shawl. After this, Dimple sat on the ground with folded hands in front of the Shankaracharya. He reiterated his demand to declare the cow as “Rashtra Mata” (Mother of the Nation). Dimple Yadav expressed regret over the Kannauj incident and said the Shankaracharya had to spend a night on the road, adding that the party felt sorry for it. Dimple also said that SP national president Akhilesh Yadav fully supports the Shankaracharya’s campaign and will continue to do so in the future. She further remarked that the disrespect shown to the Shankaracharya during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj would be “answered by nature itself”. See 2 pictures... SP MP pays respects at the event Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand was staying at the marriage hall of former SP MLA Rajkumar Yadav in Mainpuri. He mentioned the incident in Kannauj where he had to spend the night on the roadside. Dimple Yadav told him that Akhilesh Yadav was deeply hurt over the incident, adding that if he had known earlier, proper arrangements would have been made. She also said Akhilesh had apologised to him. The Shankaracharya responded that since it was not Dimple’s fault, there was no need for an apology, but he appreciated the sensitivity shown. After about an hour-long programme, he left for Kishani. “Insult to Sanatan Dharma being witnessed” Dimple Yadav said the Shankaracharya deserved full respect and expressed concern over what she called disrespect towards Sanatan Dharma, adding that the world was witnessing it. She also criticised those in power, saying people were seeing how religious leaders were being disrespected. She compared the stature of Shankaracharyas to the four Vedas and said their dignity was very significant. Dimple added that such disrespect would be answered by nature. She reiterated that Akhilesh Yadav and the Samajwadi Party stood firmly with the Shankaracharya and his movement. Shankaracharya vows to continue movement Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand said his primary resolve is to secure constitutional recognition for declaring the cow as “Mother of the Nation”. He said the movement would continue until the demand is fulfilled. Allegations of administrative pressure Earlier on 3 June, during his yatra in Kannauj, arrangements for his night stay at a private school in Chhibramau were cancelled after alleged administrative intervention. Organisers claimed permission was withdrawn at the last moment. After this, the Shankaracharya stayed at a temporary tent set up at a roadside venue, where police remained deployed overnight. Supporters alleged lack of basic facilities like electricity and fans. He later accused the administration of harassment, saying he was forced to stay on government land after being denied accommodation. Akhilesh met Shankaracharya three months ago SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had met Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand in Lucknow on 12 March. The meeting lasted about an hour, during which Akhilesh was seen sitting on the floor before him. After the meeting, Akhilesh told the media that he had met the Shankaracharya with respect and added that “fake saints would now be exposed”. Cow protection campaign The Shankaracharya had launched his cow protection campaign from Varanasi. His journey covered several districts including Jaunpur, Sultanpur, Sitapur, and Lucknow as part of a wider outreach movement.

stories.title: Murder, loot planned on WhatsApp groups:Limbs broken for ₹500; ‘Katra Gang’ kills hotel businessman’s son
stories.summary: On the night of 29 May, in Ghazipur, the son of hotel businessman Vineet Rai was shot dead. The murder was allegedly planned on a WhatsApp group named “Katra Gang”. Everything—from how many bullets would be fired, which weapon would be used, and how the killing would be carried out—was decided in advance. This is not the first such case in Uttar Pradesh. In districts like Maharajganj, Ballia and Unnao, criminals are increasingly using WhatsApp groups to plan crimes. Whether it is extortion, assault or murder, the planning is often done on these groups. These networks have now become a major challenge for the administration. Read the report… Four members of the “Katra Gang” opened multiple rounds of firing on Vineet Rai. He was hit by four bullets and later died in hospital. Accused called himself “King of Ghazipur” In Ghazipur, Alok Rai runs a luxury hotel worth around ₹20 crore. His son Vineet used to manage the business. On 29 May, around 11 pm, four masked men arrived on two bikes. They first spoke to the guard Shambhu outside and asked for 16 bottles of beer. He told them it was available. They took 8 bottles. At that moment, Vineet came out to go home and walked towards his vehicle. As he reached his car, the attackers opened fire. The first bullet hit his hand, and he tried to run. The second hit his waist and he fell down. After that, two more bullets were fired into his chest. He was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The four accused—Shankar Pandey, Kamlesh Chaudhary, Sonu Yadav and Monu Tripathi—are absconding. Shankar Pandey is the main accused. Shankar Pandey used to upload “dreaded gangster-style” videos on YouTube. People used to comment asking him to add them to his WhatsApp group. ₹1 crore extortion demand led to murder According to Vineet’s father Alok Rai, the accused had been threatening him for the past two years and demanding extortion money. They called it “gang tax” and demanded ₹1 crore, saying the hotel was worth ₹20 crore. They had also vandalised the hotel several times. Police investigation has revealed that Shankar Pandey had formed a gang called “Katra Gang” and created a WhatsApp group with members involved in criminal activity. They projected themselves on social media as the “King of Ghazipur” and Shankar called himself a “Bahubali”. According to the family, the gang was involved in several crimes over the past two years: “Contract killing for ₹500” in Ballia In neighbouring Ballia district, youths in the Beltharoad area (PIN 221715) formed a gang and created a WhatsApp group. Inside the group, discussions reportedly included committing violent acts such as breaking someone’s arms or legs for just ₹500. The group grew to more than 70 members and carried out crimes including assault and robbery. Some members allegedly received political protection. Later, the group split into two factions. In October 2025, a dispute broke out and a young man named Ayush was shot dead. Police registered cases against four accused: Robin Singh, Pawan Singh, Rohit and Raj. Even after six months, no one associated with the group is openly active now. 28 arrested after gang clash In the Gorakhpur–Maharajganj border area, gangs named “AK-47 Gang” and “Red Gang” emerged last year. They used WhatsApp groups to organise assaults, threats and extortion. Some members even used bikes with “AK-47” written on them and gun symbols. On 27 October 2025, both groups clashed violently, leading to stone-pelting and firing. Six people were seriously injured. Police arrested 28 people, including several minors. Some were paraded in public after arrest. Young boys aged 18–22 involved in crime During the COVID period, groups like “Mahakal” and “Gunda” were formed in Gorakhpur. Young men aged 18 to 22 joined them. Between 2023 and 2024, several members were arrested for robbery and assault. Police say these groups used WhatsApp chats to plan crimes and then carried them out while portraying themselves as mafia-style figures. “Mahakal vs Mahadev” gang rivalry A senior police officer said that on 20 May, a youth was beaten at Khapadawa crossing after members gathered through WhatsApp messages. This led to rivalry between groups. Later, two youths from the Mahadev group were shot dead. They were cousins. Nine people were arrested in the case. After getting bail, some of them tried to regroup again, though most such groups are now under police surveillance. Other gangs in different districts In Kannauj, the “Bichchu Gang” became active and was involved in violent clashes. In one incident, a youth named Arbaaz died after being beaten at a swimming pool. In Auraiya, groups like “Boss Gang” and “Mada Gang” were seen posting videos on social media with weapons. In Ballia, other groups such as “Trishul”, “Choti” and “Chingari” also operated, although most were not linked to murders. Most WhatsApp-based gangs consist of very young members. Former DGP’s view Former Uttar Pradesh DGP Sulkhan Singh said this is not new. According to him, WhatsApp is just a communication tool; the real issue is the mindset of young people who commit such crimes and try to present themselves as gangsters or mafias on social media. He said many youngsters do not understand that being a “mafioso” is not something to glorify. Why young people are turning to crime Psychologist Dr Krishna Mishra said most of these offenders are between 16 and 23 years old. He said many come from unstable family environments where conflict and antisocial behaviour are common. According to him, peer influence, show-off culture, and exposure to violence gradually push some youths towards crime as a way to fulfil their needs or gain attention.

stories.title: UPERC imposes ₹7.18 lakh fine on UPPCL:Country’s biggest penalty over delay in power restoration after smart prepaid meter recharge
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (UPERC) on Friday imposed a penalty of ₹7.18 lakh on the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL). The decision was announced by a two-member bench comprising Chairperson Arvind Kumar and member Sanjay Kumar Singh. The Commission directed that the penalty amount must be deposited within 15 days. The action was taken over negligence in not restoring electricity within two hours after the recharge of smart prepaid meters. Chaos erupted in March-April In March 2026, the electricity department converted lakhs of smart meters from postpaid to prepaid mode without obtaining consumers’ consent. As soon as the balance turned negative, electricity supply was disconnected in nearly 5 lakh households across the state. Although consumers recharged their meters, many households faced delays of up to 15 days in restoration of power. The incident triggered widespread outrage and chaos across the state. Historic decision on Consumer Council's petition The Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Consumers Council filed a petition before the Commission, alleging violation of the UPERC (Standards of Performance) Regulations, 2019. After hearing the matter, the Commission observed that the electricity department had shown serious negligence in consumer services under the smart prepaid meter system. As per regulations, power must be restored within two hours of recharge, but electricity companies failed to meet this standard. Fine of 7.18 Lakhs and Response Sought The two-member bench imposed the penalty under Sections 142 and 57 of the Electricity Act, 2003, calculating ₹1 lakh per violation along with ₹6,000 per day of delay, taking the total to ₹7.18 lakh. The Commission noted that the situation calls for a “root cause analysis” to ensure such lapses do not recur in the future. It also sought a detailed explanation from the Managing Director of UPPCL within 15 days. Demand for compensation to consumers Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Consumers Council Chairman Avadhesh Kumar Verma said this is the highest penalty ever imposed by any electricity regulatory commission in the country on a power utility, which will strengthen accountability. He further stated that a demand will soon be raised for compensation for 1.93 lakh affected consumers whose electricity was restored with a delay of more than two hours after recharge.

stories.title: Yogi Govt to fill 38,000 jobs in 4 months:10,000 more recruitments likely before elections; youth outreach ahead of polls
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Yogi Adityanath government has stepped up efforts to woo young voters. The state is preparing to create a favourable political atmosphere by completing the recruitment process for more than 38,000 posts across various departments through the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC). The commission has already completed examinations and interviews for 23,668 posts in 115 departments by March 2026. Dates have also been finalised for examinations and interviews for 10,445 posts in 48 departments between June and September. In addition, application forms are currently being accepted for recruitment to 3,685 posts in several departments. Recruitment notifications for nearly 10,000 more posts are also expected to be announced in the coming days. Recruitments increased after poor Lok Sabha election results The pace of these recruitments, mainly for Group C posts, increased significantly after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Before the polls, many government departments were not sending proposals for vacant posts to the commission. After the election results fell short of expectations, a review reportedly found that unemployment and paper leaks were among the biggest reasons for youth dissatisfaction. Following this, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed all departments to immediately send proposals for filling vacant positions. As a result of this push, departments have been continuously forwarding proposals, and the government is now aiming to fill these 38,000 posts before the elections to strengthen its support among young voters. Preparation to woo youth through employment Senior journalist Anand Rai believes the government is trying to connect with young voters through its employment mission. According to him, efforts are being made to counter the narrative built by the Opposition after the Lok Sabha elections. He pointed out that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has been holding appointment-letter distribution ceremonies every month, while the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission, UPSSSC, Education Service Selection Commission and Police Recruitment Board continue to release vacancies. 9 lakh government recruitments never happened before Senior journalist Virendranath Bhatt says no government in the last 20 years has carried out recruitment on such a scale. The Yogi government claims to have recruited around 900,000 people in nine years. Recruitments for nearly 150,000 posts are currently underway through various recruitment bodies. Filling vacant government posts not only improves administrative functioning but also helps create a positive political atmosphere for the ruling party by generating employment opportunities. Completing recruitment on time is a challenge for the commission Experts say the commission has begun releasing recruitment notifications regularly after a long gap. On June 2, it released its examination and interview calendar. However, conducting examinations and interviews on time and declaring results promptly remains a major challenge for the commission. One reason is the shortage of staff. Five of the eight member positions in the commission are currently vacant. As a result, interviews often take longer to complete. A lack of employees also delays document verification. Ensuring that recruitment processes are not stalled due to legal challenges in the High Court and Supreme Court will be another significant test for the commission.
